newsitem.title: ITALY: Part of glacier above Italian resort falls.
newsitem.headline: Part of glacier above Italian resort falls.

text.p: A huge chunk of a glacier threatening the Alpine ski resort of Courmayeur for days has finally crashed into the valley but no one was hurt, the town's mayor said on Saturday.
"It fell overnight. From down here it looks like it has all fallen," Ferdinando Derriard told Reuters by telephone. "No one was hurt, there was no-one in the valley."
Derriard said reconnaissance planes were taking off to check the situation. No further details were immediately available.

Glacier experts said that 10,000 to 20,000 cubic metres of ice were poised to drop off "the nose" of a hanging glacier 4,050 metres (13,500 feet) up in the Grandes Jorasses peaks close to Mont Blanc, Europe's highest mountain.

They said the lump of ice was about 70 metres (230 feet) high, 100 metres (330 feet) across and two or three metres (seven to 10 feet) deep and was poised to detach itself from the body of the glacier as it moved forward.
